instruction: I have a list of people I owe money to, including amounts and descriptions, in list_of_debts.csv. For each person, (1) If they have a Venmo account, send the money privately with the specified amount and description. (2) If not, create an individual (non-grouped) Splitwise expense with the same details so I remember to pay them later. For Splitwise expenses, attach the PDF receipt as well. They are in the same folder as the CSV file.
notes: Flow: get passwords, log into file_system, list the home directory recursively to locate list_of_debts.csv and the PDF receipts in its folder, read the CSV, log into venmo and splitwise, then for each CSV row check Venmo (venmo.search_users with the person's email) and either send a private Venmo transaction (amount + description) or record a non-grouped Splitwise expense (payer = that person, debtor_emails = [supervisor], debt_amounts = [amount], receipt_file_path = the person's PDF, file_system_access_token). The CSV contents are not known in advance, so the problem assumes 3 rows and that debtor-1/debtor-2 have Venmo accounts while debtor-3 does not (has-venmo-account is a world fact gated by the venmo-status-known lookup predicate; at runtime the branch is chosen by whether search_users returns the user). Row facts (owes, person-email, receipt-for) are world state gated by csv-read / files-located knowledge predicates. ?share duplicates ?amt (enforced with equality) so debt_amounts = [amount] is passed explicitly, giving the supervisor the full share as the evaluation expects. supervisor-complete-task takes three distinct person parameters (non-API task records) so its precondition equals the goal conjunction; no answer is passed.
